children: Goldman Sachs expects U.S. hyperscalers to deploy $1.4T in capital in 2027 as artificial intelligence shifts from experimentation to implementation and consumer AI agents open a new phase of growth.

The estimate is above Wall Street consensus, with Goldman Sachs expecting the AI infrastructure spending cycle to remain elevated through 2027. Computing demand continues to outpace supply, while much of the infrastructure under development has already been contracted.

Eric Sheridan, a business unit leader at Goldman Sachs Research, said the shift toward implementation was a key takeaway from the bank’s Communacopia + Technology Conference in San Francisco earlier this month.

“I thought we would hear more about what companies were doing in the experimentation phase,” Sheridan said. “Most companies came with distinct examples of how they're moving from experiments with AI to implementing AI in both their internal operations and workflows and externally with their customers.”

Goldman Sachs also sees consumer AI agents moving beyond chat toward tasks such as shopping, travel bookings, and calendar management. “I think we are at the beginning of a paradigm shift,” Sheridan said, describing a move toward a “much more action-oriented relationship” with AI agents.

Goldman Sachs expects consumer AI agents to be monetized through advertising and subscriptions, while more complex tasks drive higher token usage. “The mass market for AI agents will be monetized with advertising and subscriptions, much like the way the web operates today,” Sheridan said.

Goldman Sachs said AI growth still faces constraints around memory chips, power, and land, while lower token prices will be key to driving mass adoption. “We received a lot of comments at the conference about the need for deflation in the unit pricing for tokens to drive mass adoption,” Sheridan said.

title: Goldman Sachs expects U.S. hyperscaler capex to reach $1.4T by 2027
